# requireNonBoolean

<link-summary>Returns the value after checking that it is not a boolean.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireNonBoolean() — Returns the value after checking that it is not a boolean. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireNonBoolean<T>(
  value: T | boolean,
  message: string = "Expected a non-boolean value."
): T;
```

Only the two primitives pass. `new Boolean(false)` is an object, and the strings `"true"` and `"false"` are strings.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                                  | Type           | Description                                                   |
| :--------------------------------------------------------- | :------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                                    | `T \| boolean` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a non-boolean value."` | `string`       | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`T` — the same value, with a boolean excluded from its type.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition               |
| :------------------------- | :---------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is a boolean. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireNonBoolean("true"); // => "true"
requireNonBoolean(1); // => 1
requireNonBoolean(true); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireNonBoolean(false); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
